clue.text: One main dump explodes — panic ensues

indicators.note: something that explodes is blown apart, so these three words' letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A huge rubbish tip blows up and the neighbourhood flies into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explodes' scatters the letters of ONE MAIN DUMP, which rearrange into the answer; 'ensues' just joins the definition on.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild uproar and chaos is what a crowd in a panic produces, and the word names that state of confusion.

clue.text: Ram to sire a new variety

indicators.note: a new variety of something is a fresh version of it, so these letters are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A livestock breeder plans to use a ram to sire a new breed of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new variety' rearranges SIRE A into the star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign covering late March to April is symbolised by a male sheep.

clue.text: Won't change hide-out by a little path

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the word hide are jumbled

parts.note: RD, short for road, is a path written in abbreviated, little form

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly refuses to move their hiding place beside a small footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide-out' reads as a hiding place, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on 'hide' alone, making DIEH. 'Won't change' defines a stubborn person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person who resists all reform is called this, so the phrase describes someone who refuses to alter.

clue.text: Will out?

parts.note: completes the proverb that a killing will always be discovered in the end, the clue giving only its final two words

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says that a killing cannot stay secret: it 'will out'. The clue asks what fills the gap before those words.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that an unlawful killing always comes to light eventually.

clue.text: Points me out? That's favouritism

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of points me are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone singles me out and an onlooker cries foul at the obvious bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POINTS ME into the answer; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving jobs or favours to relatives is a particular kind of bias toward one's own.

clue.text: Luke Lee awkwardly plucking it?

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means doing it clumsily and out of order, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Luke Lee fumbles as he tries to pluck a small stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges LUKE LEE into the answer, and the whole clue pictures someone strumming the instrument. The usual spelling is UKULELE; this variant is also recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: The small four-stringed guitar from Hawaii is played by plucking or strumming.

clue.text: Great humiliation if I can't moor it up the creek

indicators.note: being up the creek means being in a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A boater would be terribly embarrassed if unable to tie up the boat in a muddy creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the creek' rearranges IF I CANT MOOR IT into the answer; the fodder needs three Is, so an I has dropped out of the scanned text.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep shame and embarrassment are what this word names, as when one's pride is badly wounded.

clue.text: Secure list to gaming board

parts.note: to pin something is to fasten or secure it
a table is a list of figures or data set out in rows

explanation.surface: Instructions for fastening a list onto a board used for games.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin-table is an old British name for a pinball machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinball machine is a sloping table used for playing games of chance and skill.

clue.text: Play with fruit or vegetable

parts.note: a cherry is a small stone fruit
taken as written
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A grocer is asked whether a dish comes with fruit or vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Chekhov drama; 'Play' reads at first as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's last drama, about an estate and its trees being sold, is a famous stage work.

clue.text: Nothing likely to cause a shock — just fruit

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
a live wire carries current and can give an electric shock

explanation.surface: A dietary warning: nothing alarming here, it is only fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily stone fruit of a Mediterranean tree is eaten whole or pressed for oil.

clue.text: Needing to fill up again, traveller's given boy his change

parts.note: a rep, a travelling sales representative, is a commercial traveller
Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard

indicators.note: change here means alter, so the letters of the word his are reordered

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman lets a lad handle his small change when they need to stock up.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'change' sounds like coins, but it reorders 'his' into ISH. 'Needing to' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To restock or top up something that has run low is to refill it.

clue.text: Trial meant alteration of will

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: an alteration is a change, so the letters of the word meant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A court hearing was meant to settle a change to someone's will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' looks like a verb in the surface but is the legal document; 'alteration of' turns 'meant' into AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's last formal document disposing of their property is their testament.

clue.text: Trees replanted in the compound

indicators.note: trees that are replanted are moved and set down again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gardeners move some trees within an enclosed estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replanted' rearranges TREES; 'compound' suggests an enclosure but means a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an organic chemical formed from an acid and an alcohol, often fruity smelling.

clue.text: Ballet front

definitions.meaning: the Walton and Ashton ballet of that name, set to William Walton's music
the outward face of a building, or a false show put on

explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Ashton's ballet to Walton's music shares the name of a building's face.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal face of a building is its front, and Ashton's ballet bears the same title.

clue.text: Shell — and the vehicle moves so fast

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace is an old word meaning quickly or fast

explanation.surface: A car speeds along, protected by a hard outer casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves so' is a link: the car travels at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard upper covering of a tortoise or crab is its protective casing.

clue.text: Congregation may bless converts

indicators.note: to convert something is to change it into another form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A priest may bless the people who have converted to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like religious newcomers, but it rearranges MAY BLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people, as for worship, is a meeting of a body together.

clue.text: To summarize — whip the Spanish fruit

parts.note: to summarize is to sum up, and in a down light the word sum written upward reads MUS
a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A brief summing-up: whip some Spanish fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To summarize' is 'sum up': in this down light SUM is written going up, giving MUS. CAT is the cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet grape, or the raisin made from it, used for dessert wine.

clue.text: Coat of arms featuring a devil with twisted ears

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of ears are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heraldic shield shows a little devil with crumpled ears.
explanation.walkthrough: An impresa is strictly a personal emblem rather than full heraldry, so 'Coat of arms' is a loose but fair definition; 'twisted' makes RESA from 'ears'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem or heraldic device with a motto, borne as a personal badge.

clue.text: The heroic sort — he's one who succeeds

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange in a fresh order, so the letters of heroic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heroic type is described as someone who succeeds in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like 'kind' in the surface but rearranges HEROIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint heir inherits alongside another, succeeding to an estate on a death.

clue.text: A row going badly on Dee — upset by plants in the water

indicators.note: in a down light, on means placed after the piece before
something going badly goes wrong, so the letters of a row are jumbled
upset means overturned, so in this down light the word Dee is read backwards

explanation.surface: Rowers on the River Dee make a poor showing, capsizing among the weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales; the surface pictures rowers capsizing on it. 'going badly' scrambles 'A row', 'upset' turns 'Dee' over, and in a down light 'on' means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brown seaweed such as kelp grows in coastal seawater.

clue.text: The writing that takes a second a stroke

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: Handwriting where each letter takes only a second per pen stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' suggests a pen stroke but is the swimming crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy, hurried handwriting is called this kind of writing.

clue.text: Increased gratuity required to secure these seats

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such seats, not a plural noun

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity
up means raised or increased

explanation.surface: A bigger tip is needed to reserve these seats.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip-up seats fold up when not in use, as in a theatre or cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre and cinema chairs whose bottoms fold upward are described as being of this type.

clue.text: Hurl rock into the charabanc — get this insect!

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a charabanc is an old motor coach for outings

indicators.note: to hurl is to fling, so the letters of rock are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone throws a rock into an outing coach to squash a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurl' rearranges ROCK into CKRO, which goes 'into' COACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, scuttling brown pest found in kitchens is a common household insect.

clue.text: Hill-dweller about to uncover cave

parts.note: an ant lives in an anthill
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An ant is about to discover a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRE is a poetic word for a cave, used by Shakespeare in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic literary word names a cavern or hollow in rock.

clue.text: Her actors replaced some other players

indicators.note: replaced means put back in different places, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her actors were swapped for another set of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges HER ACTORS; the 'other players' are musicians, not actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of instrumental musicians is a group of performers.

clue.text: Note book Her Majesty put down

parts.note: E is a musical note
NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen writes down a note in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' means to record in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something in a ledger or register is to write it in.

clue.text: Prisoner back on the run pinching a pound — full of bile

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the organ holding bile, not an adjective

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight inside, so one piece sits within the others
back means the word for the prisoner is read in reverse

parts.note: a lag is a convict, a prisoner
a ladder is a run in a stocking or tights
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: An escaped convict steals a pound while on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the run' looks like escape, but 'the run' is a ladder in tights. 'back' makes GAL; 'pinching' holds the pound sign inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This small organ under the liver stores bile until it is needed for digestion.
